clue.text: Girl carrying free bleaching powder

indicators.note: the girl's name holds the word for free inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: Chloe is a girl's name
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A young woman is hauling a bag of bleach she got for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Chloride of lime is the old name for bleaching powder; 'carrying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloride of lime was the standard household bleach powder, so the chemical name stands for it.

clue.text: Lively as a bird

explanation.surface: Something is described as being as lively as a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful and perky people are lively; birds chirp, so a bird's song is a chirpy sound.

clue.text: Many a poem has weight — an attractive thing

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
an ode is a lyric poem
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A lot of poetry carries heavy weight, which makes it appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attractive' is meant literally: magnetic iron ore pulls metal towards it.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetite naturally attracts iron, so it is literally a thing that attracts.

clue.text: It links the shrouds as Jack rises with a rope

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for Jack is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Jack tar, or tar, is a nickname for a sailor
a line is a rope on board ship

explanation.surface: A sailor climbs aloft on the rigging with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns the sailor upward in this down clue. Shrouds are the ropes bracing a mast; the small cross-ropes forming a ladder between them are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the short ropes lashed across a ship's rigging as ladder steps, joining the stays.

clue.text: The onset of gloom in a fearful lament

indicators.note: the first letter goes inside the word for fearful

parts.note: dire means dreadful, fearful

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its beginning, so take its first letter

explanation.surface: Gloom starts to descend during a frightening song of mourning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The onset of' takes G from 'gloom'; 'in' places it inside DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral song of mourning is a lament.

clue.text: Second best comedian?

parts.note: the cream is the best part of anything

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the runner-up is the top comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals a definition by example: a very funny person is called a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilariously funny person is informally called a scream, which a good comic should be.

clue.text: Honour the girl as a holder of drink

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award
Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is given an award and stands holding a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet or communion cup is a vessel for wine.

clue.text: Without one way to subsist

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, without, as in ex dividend
I is the Roman numeral one
St, for street, is a way

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how to get by with no single means of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to live or be, at a bare minimum.

clue.text: Played impish tricks, watched by brother

indicators.note: by means beside, so the words for watched and brother stand side by side

parts.note: a monk is a religious brother
eyed means watched

explanation.surface: Someone fooled around mischievously while their brother looked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Messing about mischievously, like an ape, is fooling around.

clue.text: Girl has raw skin, having literally erred

parts.note: a miss is a girl
a pelt is an untreated animal skin

explanation.surface: A girl with chapped skin has made a mistake in writing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' means in letters: the error is in spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the letters of a word wrong is a spelling mistake, an error made in letters.

clue.text: Lack of definition in resolution

parts.note: determination means resolve, resolution

explanation.surface: Someone notes a vagueness in a formal motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution' suggests a meeting's motion, but it is firmness of purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagueness or indefiniteness is a state of being not fixed or settled.

clue.text: Fishy prawn starter is caught in the Orient

indicators.note: a starter is the first course, so the word's first letter

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A prawn cocktail first course gets netted in the Far East, smelling suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' gives P from 'prawn'. Each of 'is', 'caught', 'in' and 'the Orient' then gives letters in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Piscine means relating to or like fish, from Latin piscis.

clue.text: One of nine perhaps knocked out by the cheese

definitions.text: One of nine perhaps knocked out by the cheese

parts.words: One of nine perhaps knocked out by the cheese
parts.note: in the pub game, nine pins are bowled over by a heavy disc called the cheese

explanation.surface: Something among nine is flattened by a lump of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pub skittles the thrown wooden disc is called a cheese; nine pins stand to be knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: The pins in British pub skittles are set up in a diamond of nine and toppled by the thrown disc.

clue.text: A way to estimate value avoiding extremes

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
to rate is to assess the worth of

explanation.surface: A method for valuing something moderately.
explanation.definitionFit: Being measured and not going too far either way is avoiding extremes.

clue.text: Sapwood to incinerate in a chimney for Jock

indicators.note: the word for incinerate goes inside the Scots chimney with its article

parts.note: lum is Scots for chimney; Jock is a nickname for a Scot
to burn is to incinerate

explanation.surface: A Scotsman uses the chimney to burn sapwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'for Jock' tells you the word is Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Alburnum is the botanical term for the soft outer wood of a tree, beneath the bark.

clue.text: To invest in New Eden is upper class

indicators.note: the letter for upper class goes inside the rearranged letters
new suggests the word Eden made afresh, its letters reshuffled

parts.note: U is the classic label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Someone notes that putting money into a new paradise is posh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges EDEN to ENDE; 'in' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or clothe someone with a quality, as one invests a person with power.

clue.text: May's dread — wild abstractions

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters running loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A woman named May has a terrible fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' jumbles MAYS and DREAD together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lost in reverie is a state of abstraction, absent-minded fancy.

clue.text: Salesman gets tight and is superseded

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a travelling salesman
laced, as in a corset, is pulled tight

explanation.surface: A salesman gets drunk and loses his job to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like drunk, but here it is laced, as of a corset.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to take its place.

clue.text: Smooth society betting term

parts.note: even means level, smooth

explanation.surface: A suave club phrase for gambling odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens are odds of one to one, where a winning bet doubles the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Even money is a bookmaker's phrase for odds where the win equals the stake.

clue.text: Holy man deceived — went a bit off course

parts.note: S, for saint, is a holy man
kidded means fooled, deceived

explanation.surface: A saint was tricked and strayed slightly from his path.
explanation.definitionFit: A car sliding sideways on ice veers off its line.

clue.text: How one may reach next round without a fight, incidentally

definitions.text: How one may reach next round without a fight
definitions.meaning: advancing in a tournament because no opponent was drawn
by the way, as a passing remark

explanation.surface: A boxer advances without a contest, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: A bye lets a player go through to the next round with no opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing to the next round unopposed comes by way of a bye; the phrase also means by the way.

clue.text: Miss after a name in the city? Shut up!

indicators.note: after says the word for miss comes after the first part
the letter for a name sits inside the city's postcode

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London
N is the abbreviation for name
to lose is to miss, as with a chance

explanation.surface: A young woman follows a famous name in town and is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' means to pen in, not to be quiet. EC is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut something up is to confine or surround it.

clue.text: Musical exercises are key to duets, perhaps

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters of duets could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Practice pieces are said to be the secret to playing duets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges DUETS to TUDES; 'are' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Studies written to train technique are what musicians practise.

clue.text: One result that might produce more stout

indicators.note: the clue words might yield something else if their letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single outcome could make for a fuller, stronger beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that might produce' anagrams I and RESULT. 'stout' tempts as the beer, but it means sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means sturdy and vigorous, and lusty means strong and hearty.

clue.text: Man of austerity thus about to …

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for thus goes around the next word

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus

explanation.surface: A hardy man is about to speak, then trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on to the next clue but adds nothing to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Greek philosophy endured hardship without complaint.

clue.text: Damned dogs in play

indicators.note: the word for dogs goes inside the word for play

parts.note: an act is part of a play, or a play in the sense of acting
curs are mongrel dogs

explanation.surface: Wretched hounds appear on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under a curse, a person is doomed.

clue.text: …remove joint name from bank ledger

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a joint account holder to be taken off the ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' and 'name' are part of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and leg.

clue.text: The Utopia to which 16 dn, may take one?

definitions.text: The Utopia to which 16 dn, may take one?

parts.words: The Utopia to which 16 dn, may take one?
parts.note: 16 down is the answer to another clue, and its reveries carry you off to an imaginary realm in the sky

explanation.surface: Where daydreaming might transport someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Aristophanes' play The Birds, where birds build a city in the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealised, impossible fantasy world is the stuff of idle reverie.

clue.text: Determine to dump detectives in the river

indicators.note: the detectives are dropped inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in England, Wales and Scotland
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: A gang decides to throw the police into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dump' is part of the picture. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle on a choice is to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Delivers documents for publication

explanation.surface: A firm sends out press handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to set free; press statements issued to newspapers are handouts for print.
